newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-PAPER ON PITCH DELAYS ARGENTINE MATCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PAPER ON PITCH DELAYS ARGENTINE MATCH.

text.p: Fans at an Argentine championship match threw so much paper onto the pitch in their traditional "ticker tape" reception on Sunday that the players could not play on it.

The start of the Buenos Aires derby between Racing Club and Independiente was delayed for half an hour while the field was cleared of paper, which had been thrown from the terraces as the players entered the arena.
Referee Javier Castrilli, famous in Argentina for his rigid approach to the game, claimed that otherwise the pitch would have been unfit for play.

The "ticker tape" reception, in which pieces of paper rain down from the terraces, is traditional in Argentine soccer and at big games provides one of the most spectacular sights in international sport.
Fans showed their displeasure at the delay by throwing stones and other objects onto the pitch.
Once play got under way, Independiente, coached by Cesar Luis Menotti, recorded their first win of the season thanks to a last minute strike by Jose Luis Calderon, who also opened the scoring.
Crisis-hit Boca Juniors, the most popular team in Argentina, finished with nine men as they crashed 4-0 to San Lorenzo, leaving them with only four points from their first four games.
Veteran midfielder Nestor Gorosito and former Brazil international Silas scored two goals each.
Boca had Julio Toresani and Nestor Lorenzo sent off in a three minute spell while veteran defender and former Argentina captain Oscar Ruggeri was also dismissed.
Champions River Plate maintained their perfect record by beating Huracan 3-0. They have not conceeded a goal in their four wins.
